heading: Marijuana Establishments: Grounds for Denial of Application for Licensure

contentTree.heading: Marijuana Establishments: Grounds for Denial of Application for Licensure

children.content:
Each of the following, in and of itself, constitutes full and adequate grounds for denying an
applicant on an application for a Marijuana Establishment License and the associated individuals
and entities, but not for the renewal of a License.

The applicant failed to complete the application process within the time required by the
Commission.

Information provided by the applicant was deceptive, misleading, false or fraudulent, or that
tends to deceive or create a misleading impression, whether directly, or by omission or
ambiguity, including lack of disclosure or insufficient disclosure.

The application indicates an inability to maintain and operate a Marijuana Establishment
in compliance with the requirements of St. 2016, c. 334, as amended by St. 2017, c. 55, {{extref:M.G.L.
c. 94G}}, and 935 CMR 500.00 including, but not limited to, {{ref:500.105}} and {{ref:500.110}}, based on the submission of information required by {{ref:500.101(1)}}.

The applicant has been determined to be unsuitable pursuant to any one or more of the
factors listed in {{ref:500.800}} and {{ref:500.801}}.

The applicant failed to comply with the control limitations listed in 935CMR {{ref:500.050(1)(b)}}
or would likely fail to comply with such limitations if a License were granted.

An applicant had its License or registration revoked or application denied in the
Commonwealth or an Other Jurisdiction.

Any other ground that serves the purposes of St. 2016, c. 334, as amended by St. 2017,
c. 55, {{extref:M.G.L. c. 94G}}, or {{ref:500.000}}.
